title: Unified Composable Artifact System
description: Introduce a first-class composition/reference primitive so every artifact is either composable (owned child, own ArtifactEnvelope/ArtifactVcs history, aggregated by the parent via a CompositionCoordinator) or referenceable (independent ArtifactLink with pin semantics), fully integrated with the existing CQRS mutation-based event-sourcing stack (envelope/store/vcs/spr/backbone/hub) — atomic cross-envelope gestures via one InvocationResult/UndoGroup, cascading checkpoints, graceful degradation for sync. Dissolve all duplicated plugin content types (9+ mesh types, 4 brep topologies, 3 path-segment vocabularies, 2 LocalizedText, duplicate kind ids, emoji ids) into the stdio plugin's neutral 🧿️semio artifact, expanding its subset roster from 13 to 18 (rename workflow→flow, object→value; add text/table/object/graph/kit) with an enforced composition DAG. Unify artifact identity onto one grammar (s.<plugin>.<artifact>) and collapse the current 6 manual registration channels into a single declare_artifact! macro. Migrate all 33 plugins to compose/reference stdio artifacts instead of redefining content types. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/the-current-artifact-system-eager-scone.md. Execution: 7 waves (W0 recon, W1 kernel primitives + coordinator, W2 stdio roster, W3 three exemplar plugins, W4 mass fan-out across ~29 remaining plugins at parallel width 7, W5 hot-file serializer, W6 policy/taxonomy ratchet, W7 verify+close) run via parallel Claude Code agents and background Workflows, interleaved with the concurrently-running SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL ticket via a per-plugin wave2-report clearance oracle. Greenfield: no compatibility layers, no legacy support, fixtures regenerated not upcast.
summary: Implemented composable/referenceable artifact primitives (ArtifactRef/ArtifactChild/ArtifactLink/CompositionCoordinator/group undo) over CQRS event-sourcing, froze stdio's 18-subset semio roster, proved the pattern on 3 exemplars (lowpoly/cad/writer), then fanned it out across ~26 of ~29 plugins - each independently re-verified by the orchestrator (real cargo check/cargo nextest re-runs, not trusted from agent self-reports), catching and fixing several real misclassifications along the way (a repo-wide fake-auto-commit-date trap that had produced two false "pre-existing, two months old" claims; a false "tests pass" claim in block's report; norm's flawed "composition would break granularity" round-1 reasoning, corrected with a working round 2). Landed a working migration-recipe.md that captured two real framework capabilities discovered live during the fan-out (ArtifactView::with_children/ChildContentView resolver seam; DslField for ArtifactChild<S>) so later agents could use them instead of always hand-rolling workarounds. W5 applied every safe in-scope sharedFileRequests item to shared hot files (glue.rs mounts, one extern-crate cleanup). W6 added 3 composition policies to script.ts (canonical artifact-kind grammar, child-slot ownership-graph acyclicity, dissolved-kind-redefinition ratchet) - verified 0 breaches on the DAG/redefinition checks, proving the migration wave produced a clean composition graph. W7 final health: framework-plugin (W1 kernel) clean with all 11 composition law tests passing; stdio clean, 3001/3006 tests passing (5 pre-existing failures, none in composition territory, matching independently-disclosed concurrent-session debt). Several plugins (fem, norm, block, puzzle, architect) landed honest, fully-verified partial completions rather than forced full migrations, each with a precise documented continuation path. demonstrator was held for the entire ticket - the one plugin in the original map with zero UCAS work - because a separate concurrent session actively rebuilding it explicitly asked to hold. Extensive live cross-session coordination throughout with DKM (DISSOLVE-KERNELS-AND-MODULES), APA, #2553 (ENGINELESS-ARTIFACTS), and a demonstrator-restoration session - including catching and correcting the fake-commit-date bug in my own and DKM's methodology, and a live design ruling on their math-module dissolution's roster-freeze question.
